audit.whatIsWrong: Level chart said Jax at Level 1, First item and 2+ items. The packet chart, the prose (whys[0] 'your weakest window'; whys[5] 'the duel begins tilting his way'; whys[6]/late 'lane slips away') and the already-audited mirror all disagree.
audit.why: Mirror (kassadin__jax) set First item = Skill and 2+ items = Kassadin. Level 1 with only Leap Strike against an escape-less Kassadin is even, not a Jax win.
audit.corrected: phases[0]/win[0] = Skill, phases[5]/win[5] = Skill, phases[6]/win[6] = Kassadin, proposed as one atomic group across both layers. Levels 2-5 and Level 6 left alone.

audit.whatIsWrong: Riftwalk was described only as 'dropping fast' with no number, and breakdown.cooldowns treated it as a cooldown you can catch down late.
audit.why: Riftwalk is 5/3.5/2s base. At rank 1 there is a real 5s window; by rank 3 it is 2s and effectively never down — the real limiter is its stacking mana cost, not its cooldown.
audit.corrected: Real numbers written into spikes[2].text and breakdown.cooldowns; Counter Strike's 17s at rank 1 added.

audit.whatIsWrong: report[5] and breakdown.cooldowns implied Counter Strike is a general answer to Kassadin's commit ('E-counter his KA').
audit.why: Riot's text: Counter Strike dodges incoming ATTACKS. Almost all of Kassadin's damage is spells — Null Sphere, Force Pulse and Riftwalk land at full value through it. Only his autos, including the Nether Blade reset, are wasted. The mirror audit reached the same conclusion.
audit.corrected: report[5] and breakdown.cooldowns rewritten to state that Counter Strike eats the Nether Blade auto only, and that Null Sphere and Force Pulse pass through.

audit.whatIsWrong: dontsFull[2].t 'Force fights before your item spike' carried a description about burning E — copy-paste mismatch.
audit.why: The description did not describe the don't it sits under.
audit.corrected: Description replaced with the actual two-item scaling reason.

audit.why: 50.78% over 768 games matches the EVEN diff label.
Kassadin's passive reduces magic damage, which the early block already leans on correctly (physical Leap Strike over magic ticks).

edits.before: Yours from level 1. See the level-by-level chart for the swing points.
edits.after: Even at 1, yours from 2 to 5, his once items land. See the full chart.

edits.before: Track Kassadin's Riftwalk: His mobility spike at 6. Kill him before it scales. When it is down — E-counter his KA, Q-W burst.
edits.after: Counter Strike dodges attacks, not spells: it eats his Nether Blade auto, while Null Sphere and Force Pulse land at full value through it.

edits.before: - Kassadin Riftwalk: matchup-defining — His mobility spike at 6. Kill him before it scales. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Riftwalk: 5s at rank 1, 2s at rank 3 — late it is never down, so punish its stacking mana cost instead. - Counter Strike: 17s at rank 1, and it eats his autos only. - Leap Strike: 8s, your commit.

edits.before: Your Trinity Force on-hit spike still out-duels his first AP item, but his Riftwalk cooldown is dropping fast — only commit the all-in when his blink is on cooldown, or he just walks out of your stun.
edits.after: Your Trinity Force on-hit spike trades even with his first AP item, but Riftwalk is 5s at rank 1 and 3.5s at rank 2 — commit in the seconds right after he blinks, or he simply steps out of your stun.

edits.before: Burning E on nothing — your counter-stun is the matchup; without it you are a man with a lamppost.
edits.after: Past two items his Riftwalk rotation beats your duel outright — fight only with vision and your team set.
